'''Virtual Original''' is the [[Players Committee]] Virtual-card era from the first Virtual Set through the [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]]. The first set became tournament-legal on 9 March 2002.<ref name="decivs1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], decipher.com (Wayback, 10 June 2002 snapshot; dated 5 March 2002)</ref> Printable overlays from this era are [[V-slips]]. Constructed cutoffs are listed under [[Formats#Original Virtual constructed (2002–2009)|Formats]].

== Beginnings ==

The Players Committee took over organized play after [[Decipher]] ended the commercial game in 2001. [[Warren Holland]] outlined the committee on ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' on 28 December 2001. The first Player Advocates were named on 25 January 2002.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002; letter dated 25 January 2002)</ref>

[[Players Committee-Lucasfilm agreement|Lucasfilm limits]] required free electronic cards, with no new film images and no physical PC cards.<ref name="pcabout">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/about-us/ About Us], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020234816/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/about-us.html Internet Archive]</ref> The first Virtual Card Set was announced on 12 February 2002, targeting a 4 March 2002 community release.<ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net, 12 February 2002 (citing Game Players Network). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020214905/https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Internet Archive]</ref> Twelve [[Premiere]]-based slips became tournament-legal on Saturday, 9 March 2002.<ref name="decivs1" />

== How Virtual cards worked ==

Players printed PDF slips, cut them, and sleeved them over matching Decipher cards.<ref name="tfn2002" /><ref name="decivs1" /> Virtual versions used a '''(V)''' mark in rulings, articles, and deck lists.<ref name="decivs1" /> A deck could include both the original Decipher text and the (V) version. A player could not switch a card either way once a tournament began.<ref name="decivs1" />

== Online play ==

[[Holotable]] launched in late 2004 as a downloaded virtual tabletop.<ref name="ringer">[https://www.theringer.com/2018/5/21/17374528/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community The Force Is Strong With This 'Star Wars' Subculture], Ben Lindbergh, ''The Ringer'', 21 May 2018. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20180523173054/https://www.theringer.com/2018/5/21/17374528/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community Internet Archive]</ref> Players enforced the rules themselves. Holodeck was the companion deck builder.<ref name="c1ght">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/holotable-playing-star-wars-ccg-online-the-setup/ Holotable - Playing Star Wars CCG Online - The Setup], Category One Games. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20220926090936/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/holotable-playing-star-wars-ccg-online-the-setup/ Internet Archive]</ref> TheForce.Net hosted Holotable from January 2007 and posted twelve preconstructed decks on 9 April 2007.<ref name="tfn2007">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Preconstructed_Decks_Now_Available_For_Online_Star_Wars_CCG_104875.asp Pre-constructed Decks Now Available For Online Star Wars CCG], TheForce.Net, 9 April 2007. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20071030072612/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Preconstructed_Decks_Now_Available_For_Online_Star_Wars_CCG_104875.asp Internet Archive]</ref> Those decks named a Classic list and a Saga list of all cards. Saga required a Starting Effect to use [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]].<ref name="tfn2007" />

== Sites and distribution ==

An official site at swccgpc.com carried news by October 2002.<ref name="swccgpc2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106101746/http://www.swccgpc.com/ The SWCCG Player's Committee], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 6 November 2002)</ref> On 10 June 2009 the Players Committee moved to StarWarsCCG.org.<ref name="domain2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102740/http://www.starwarsccg.org/news/news.php?id=69 New Domain and Server], starwarsccg.org news.php?id=69 (posted 10 June 2009; Wayback, 6 July 2009)</ref> A 2008 Icon Guide from the Players Committee names the numbered Virtual Sets.<ref name="iconguide">[http://karcianki.pl/files/sw/Icon%20Guide.pdf SWCCG Icon Guide] (karcianki.pl host; PC 2008 imprint). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195537/http://karcianki.pl/files/sw/Icon%20Guide.pdf Internet Archive]</ref>

== Sets ==

The program issued numbered Virtual Sets 1 through 17 plus [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]]. Legal days and PDF rows are on [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]. Fifth Anthology was previewed as Virtual Set 18 in June 2009. Its preview cards shipped inside Reflections IV, later [[Virtual Block 6]].<ref name="plfifth">[https://star-wars.pl/News/10466,Preview_Fifth_Anthology.html Preview Fifth Anthology], star-wars.pl, 8 June 2009. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250620070924/https://star-wars.pl/News/10466,Preview_Fifth_Anthology.html Internet Archive]</ref> [[Virtual Set 19: Galaxy At War]] was planned and never released.<ref name="plsets">[https://star-wars.pl/Tekst/1963,Star_Wars_CCG_Virtual_Sets.html Star Wars CCG - Virtual Sets], star-wars.pl. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192957/https://star-wars.pl/Tekst/1963,Star_Wars_CCG_Virtual_Sets.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== End of the era ==

In 2009 the Players Committee regrouped the numbered sets into six thematic Virtual Blocks.<ref name="blockreorg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf VirtualBlock1.pdf] (official text as of 7 December 2009). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020181626/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf Internet Archive]</ref> That change opened the [[Virtual Legacy]] era.
